thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: KV cache memory spike detected in prod-west-1 (alerts: kv-cache.free_mem < 10%) :rotating_light:
oncall-alex: I'm paged, joining. seeing elevated p50/p99 latency for text-generation routes.
sre-jen: confirming - Grafana shows KV cache resident set jump at 03:14 UTC, correlates with continuous-batching throughput spike.
eng-runtime-mike: ETA to look is 5m. adding context: we rolled a batching tweak to reduce RPCs yesterday, could be interacting with allocator.
infra-katie: I can pull node-level nvidia-smi + dmesg across the pool. starting aggregates.
oncall-alex: customer-ops-lina any user reports?
customer-ops-lina: Two customers opened support tickets citing intermittent 503s and slow responses since ~03:10. escalating to account owners.
sre-jen: quick mitigation idea: throttle continuous batching concurrency and fall back to smaller batch size. preferably via runtime flag so no restart. can we toggle?
eng-runtime-mike: We have a dynamic config endpoint. Pushing conservative defaults: batch.max_tokens=1024 -> 512, batch.max_concurrency=128 -> 64. applying to prod-west-1 canary first.
deploy-bot: config update queued: /cfg/set prod-west-1 batch.max_tokens=512 batch.max_concurrency=64 (canary target subset nodes)
oncall-alex: canary applied to 3/30 nodes. monitoring.
sre-jen: after canary, memory pressure on those nodes dropped ~18% and latency improved. but other nodes still climbing.
eng-runtime-mike: rolling the config to remaining nodes now. doing 5-node waves with 30s gap.
eng-runtime-mike: while rolling, I want heap and allocator stats from an affected host. @infra-katie can you run the diagnostic script and attach output?
infra-katie: running:
```
ssh prod-west-1-node-42 'sudo /opt/redwood/bin/kv-heap-stats --json > /tmp/kvstats.json && tail -n 200 /var/log/syslog | grep -i oom'
cat /tmp/kvstats.json
```
infra-katie: paste: arena_total: 142GB, arena_free: 4GB, fragmentation_ratio: 0.78, slab_count: 4213, largest_free_block: 24MB
oncall-alex: fragmentation_ratio 0.78 is bad. looks like allocator is scattering small allocations. correlates with lots of small batch prefetches.
sre-jen: also seeing repeated ptorch/cuda malloc slowdowns in logs: 
```
2026-03-15T03:12:09Z WARN cuda_malloc: slow alloc 125ms size=48MB ctx=worker-17
2026-03-15T03:12:10Z WARN cuda_malloc: slow alloc 210ms size=64MB ctx=worker-22
```
eng-runtime-mike: Those slow cuda mallocs can stall batching threads, increasing KV cache concurrency and fragmenting arenas. two-pronged approach: 1) reduce batch concurrency (we're doing it), 2) trigger arena compaction / defrag for affected processes.
infra-katie: we can send USR1 to runtime to attempt on-the-fly compaction. prepping a safe command: `sudo pkill -SIGUSR1 -f redwood-runtime` will notify processes and run compaction in-place. want me to run across all nodes?
oncall-alex: hold - we should hit canary nodes first and validate no crash.
sre-jen: agreed. run on 3 canary nodes. if compaction completes and memory drops, escalate to rest. compaction script also logs compaction events, so we can verify.
infra-katie: compaction started on canary nodes. logs: `arena_compact: freed 6.4GB in 12s; fragmentation_ratio now 0.41`
eng-runtime-mike: good signal. continuing config rollout and scheduling compaction on next wave after config change applied per node.
customer-ops-lina: customers reporting improvement for some requests. still seeing intermittent failures for longer prompts.
sre-jen: let's enable a fallback model variant with smaller context windows for affected routes to reduce KV pressure. eng-runtime-mike can you add route-level fallback?
eng-runtime-mike: adding per-route fallback: /v1/generate -> model: redwood-alpha-2x -> redwood-alpha-1x (shorter kv footprint). will route only when per-request kv cache usage > threshold. deploying rule now.
eng-runtime-mike: rule deployed. observed immediate drop in long-tail p99 latency for generate route.
eng-runtime-mike: however, one node (prod-west-1-node-17) still shows fragmentation creeping back after compaction. suspect a memory leak in allocator path for repeated small allocations. capturing heap-profile.
infra-katie: capturing tcmalloc and pmap, uploading to /tmp/leak-dump-node-17.tar.gz
sre-jen: assigning to eng-runtime-mike and infra-katie for on-call deep-dive. paging out-of-band to eng-runtime oncall.
oncall-alex: customer impact summary for pager: ~8% of requests experienced 5-20s extra latency or 503s between 03:10-03:40 UTC. affected customers: 2 enterprise tenants (notified). no data loss. SLA risk: low-medium; we're continuing monitoring.
eng-runtime-mike: temporary mitigation checklist:
- throttled batching concurrency (done)
- decreased batch max tokens (done)
- on-the-fly arena compaction (canary -> rolling)
- route-level fallback (deployed)
- capturing heap and cuda malloc traces for root cause

sre-jen: next steps: prioritize allocator regression: reproduce with stress test (small repeated prefetches + high concurrency) in staging. add telemetry for malloc latencies and per-arena fragmentation over time.
eng-runtime-mike: I will add more verbose allocator telemetry and a circuit-breaker to limit continuous-batching growth if malloc latency spikes. planning a small hotfix to runtime in next patch window.
infra-katie: for immediate safety, I rolled a node-level oom_kill protection change (cgroup memory.high tweak) to prevent single process from starving GPU memory for other tenants. This buys time but not a root fix.
sre-jen: good. want on-call handoff at 07:00 UTC for follow-through. Alex, will you hand off to night team?
oncall-alex: yep. I'll post a concise handoff with links to timelines, dumps, and customers.
eng-runtime-mike: rough RCA hypothesis (WIP): recent batching change increased frequency of small prefetch allocations which interacts poorly with allocator heuristics + intermittent slow cuda allocations -> threads stall and accumulate outstanding requests -> arenas fragment -> memory pressure -> increased latency & 503s.
customer-ops-lina: I sent incident notes to affected customer admins and scheduled a 1:1 debrief for tomorrow.
incident-bot: Incident severity reduced to SEV-2 after mitigations.
oncall-alex: Handoff note: joining the 07:00 UTC oncall rotation to monitor. primary owners: eng-runtime-mike (allocator fix), infra-katie (heap traces & node safety), sre-jen (monitoring & postmortem).
sre-jen: I'll open a follow-up bug with dumps attached and tag for allocator team. also propose a runbook entry: "kv-arena-compaction-on-sigusr1" with safe thresholds and rollout steps.
eng-runtime-mike: will prototype a runtime patch that monitors cuda_malloc latency spikes and auto-reduces continuous-batching concurrency; aiming for PR today and staged test tomorrow.
infra-katie: uploading collected artifacts: /artifacts/1765554321/node-17-leak-dump.tar.gz, /artifacts/1765554321/kvstats.csv
oncall-alex: thanks everyone. closing thread for now; we'll reconvene if anything regresses.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: all canary nodes stable for 25m, continuing to monitor.
keywords: kv cache, allocator, fragmentation, cuda malloc, compaction, continuous batching, on-call, mitigation, canary, config roll
